audits.resolution_reason: Strict distinct-size validator rejects three of four canonical labeled pairs and sampler excludes ties. Reviewer-reported canonical-domain contradiction and missing controls/pin remain unfixed.
audits.text:
## 4c5a96f13170

**Reproduced canonical-domain contradiction.** The generator declares strictly
distinct blob sizes, labels `tied_sizes` degenerate, and rejects ties in
`self_check`.  Canonical authority does not impose that restriction: canonical
component-size multisets are `[1,2,2]`, `[1,1,2,3]`, `[1,2,4]`, and
`[2,2,2,2]`.  Consequently `self_check` rejects 3 of the 4 labelled canonical
pairs, including the test pair, while 120 sampled generated draws contained
zero tied-size cases.

The exact per-pair findings, generator hash, and generated census are in
`checks/audit/audit-probe.json`.  The audited source hash is
`c8f3531265e448d10bf9bf01d48ab1957898815a3d814119ba8e738a92ead73e`.
This restriction can teach the false invariant “all bar heights are distinct”
and excludes much of the actual task domain, even though the Racket rule can
render ties unambiguously in left-to-right order.

Public diagnostics also reproduce the missing `RULE_HASH`, two unprobed
single-token axes, four dead textures, and texture-domain overlap; see
`checks/audit/4c5a96f13170/lint.console.log` and
`defect_lint.console.log`.  I did not modify the audited generator.

triage.reason: Retain two source-bound findings-only audits: rejected negative reachability branch and canonical tied-size contradiction; neither target repaired. Reviewer-reported evidence only.
